lines.say: In 1974, a soldier was still fighting World War Two.
The war had ended twenty-nine fucking years earlier. Nobody had told him.
Planes dropped leaflets saying it was over. He figured the leaflets were an enemy trick.
His own family came with a loudspeaker. Still thought it was a trap, the bastard.

lines.say: Because the only order that counted was the one from his commanding officer.
So they found his old major, a bookseller by then, and flew him out to read the order.
Twenty-nine years. One sentence from somebody he trusted.
You've got clients out in the jungle too. Waiting on somebody they know to say the war's over.
